title: Chapter 59: Together Forever
html:
Silence filled the dance studio. In the mirror, the man recovered first. He stood over the five girls, glaring threats at them. When one began to cry, he hauled her from the floor and jabbed a finger in her face while she shook her head desperately.

Then the girl nearly as tall as Zhang Ya rose and joined him in pressuring the others. Her familiarity with the man suggested a relationship far closer than friendship. She might even have arranged for him to arrive after the teacher left.

Caught between her persuasion and his threats, the other girls finally nodded. After several more minutes of discussion, the man left. The five changed in the dressing room and followed soon afterward.

The mirror returned to normal, but the studio’s tension deepened. Cold radiated against Chen Ge’s back as though a frozen corpse were draped over him.

That’s all?

The mirror had shown only what happened inside the studio. There had to be more. A fourth-floor fall was not inevitably fatal; unless she landed on her head, Zhang Ya might have been saved.

Red Specters are born from deep resentment… Did that fat man finish Zhang Ya off because he feared exposure? The Arts Activities Center’s water system was renovated before the school closed. Could he have used it to dispose of her body?

He rejected the theory almost at once. Zhang Ya had disappeared on school grounds; the police must have investigated. Disposing of a body was not as simple as television made it look. Often, attempts at concealment created the clearest evidence.

He wanted to know what came next, but the mirror revealed nothing more. I should call Inspector Lee. This was a murder, and the academy falls within his jurisdiction. There must be a record.

As he reached for his phone, a scream erupted behind him. Zhang Ya’s hair climbed over his shoulders like a nest of snakes and coiled around his throat and chest, binding the two of them together.

“I’m not leaving. I want to help you!” Chen Ge managed before the hair choked off his breath. It tightened like a python around its prey. Perhaps, to Zhang Ya, this was the only way they could remain together. This was her idea of true love.

He had escaped the wolf’s den only to enter the tiger’s cave. Now he understood why Zhang Ya’s love letter was cursed. She did not care for living men, and the more she loved one, the more urgently she wanted him dead.

Back to back with her, his limbs too weak to resist, Chen Ge could only plead his case. “I’ll call the police. I’ll help bring everyone who hurt you to justice!”

Even to him, the promise sounded useless. Unlike the family at Ping An Apartments, Zhang Ya did not need his help taking revenge. Five of the people who had wronged her were already trapped inside chairs, almost certainly by her hand.

The gentle, graceful girl from the photograph had become a maddened specter. Chen Ge did not dare imagine what the five girls had endured before she sealed them into the chairs.

He gave up. This was how he would die. Then, as he braced himself for the end, the hair stopped tightening.

“What is it? Is someone else still unpunished?” he asked quickly, making his willingness to help unmistakable. The hair loosened as if Zhang Ya were considering the offer. Chen Ge could only wait.

Silence reclaimed the dark studio. Ten seconds later, as Chen Ge balanced on the edge of death, the door swung open and a lanky man peered inside.

At the sight of Chen Ge, his face lit with cruel excitement. The hand bearing a peony tattoo drew a fruit knife from his back pocket. To his surprise, Chen Ge smiled too, his expression saying, Finally.

“Surprised? You left clues everywhere. Scuff marks on the outer wall, fresh mud and grass on the first-floor window, footprints all through the building. You were careless, and now you’ll pay for it.”

The man was Zhang Peng. His eyes were bloodshot, his excitement feverish, and he held the knife in his uninjured hand. Yet the moment he stepped into the studio, his vicious expression collapsed. Alarm filled his face, and he retreated with wary resentment in his eyes.

Has the mirror monster taken control of his body?

Before Chen Ge could react, Zhang Peng fled down the stairs as if he had seen something terrifying. His limbs jerked at unnatural angles, making him look like a puppet dragged by invisible strings.

The hair binding Chen Ge vanished, and so did the girl behind him. A streak of red crossed the mirror. The chase had begun. As warmth returned to his frozen limbs, he grabbed his phone and backpack and sprinted for the stairs nearly as fast as Zhang Peng.

I’ll have to put the Bloody Heart Mission aside for now. If I truly win Zhang Ya’s affection, my future may become a little too exciting to survive.

Chen Ge burst from the Arts Activities Center. After a quick glance at the dark forest around him, he called Inspector Lee.

The phone rang once before it was picked up, and Inspector Lee’s voice came through. “Xiao Chen? Did you run into Zhang Peng?”

“Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy! Zhang Peng is here. And there’s something else you need to know.” Chen Ge forced out the words between breaths as he ran for the gate.

“Fu Jun, Da Yong, contact the investigation team immediately.” Inspector Lee didn’t hang up. After he gave his orders, he returned his attention to Chen Ge. “What is this other thing you want to talk about?”

“I discovered another murder case at Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy!”
